newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giants of French advert scene differ on outlook.
newsitem.headline: Giants of French advert scene differ on outlook.

text.p: The two giants of French advertising, Havas Advertising and Publicis, are voicing contrasting views on the outlook for advertising in France following the recent French parliamentary elections.
Jean-Michel Carlo, vice chairman of Havas Advertising, said on Tuesday that the change of government could be beneficial for consumption.

The new left-wing government enjoys a level of popularity among the electorate which the outgoing centre-right government did not have, he said in an interview at the International Advertising Festival here.
"The bourse has held up well and foreign investors have not pulled out," he said.

The French advertising market should at least meet the target of four percent growth this year set by the advertising industry's representative group, l'Association des Agences Conseils en Communication (AACC), Carlo said.
However, a Publicis executive attending the festival said the election had put a stop to advertising spending after a very good start to the year.
"Perhaps it will take off again in September," said the executive, who declined to be named.
He said the Socialist government's halt to the privatisation programme, started when the centre-right took power in 1993, would dampen advertising spending.
Carlo said Havas Advertising had seen no let-up in activity since the election at the beginning of this month.
"Television is doing less well but the press is doing better," he said.

Other advertising industry executives at the festival said the car sector was still in a downward spiral it entered when government incentives for the purchase of a new car, named after prime ministers Edouard Balladur and Alain Juppe who brought them in, came to an end.
"Since the Balladurette and the Juppette finished, spending on cars has slumped, with a disastrous effect on advertising strategies," said one advertising executive.
